sanskrit: pārṣṇibhiś ca kaśābhiś ca tāḍayantas turaṃgamān javam uttamam āsthāya sarvataḥ prādravan bhayāt
english: Goading their horses with heels and whips, the warriors took to their swiftest pace and fled in terror in every direction.

sanskrit: kāmbojasainyaṃ vidrāvya durjayaṃ yudhi bhārata yavanānāṃ ca tat sainyaṃ śakānāṃ ca mahad balam
english: Having routed the Kāmboja host, hard to vanquish in battle, O Bhārata, and the army of the Yavanas and the great force of the Śakas,

sanskrit: sa tataḥ puruṣavyāghraḥ sātyakiḥ satyavikramaḥ prahṛṣṭas tāvakāñ jitvā sūtaṃ yāhīty acodayat
english: that tiger among men, Sātyaki of true valour, having joyfully conquered your troops, urged his charioteer, saying, 'Drive on!'

sanskrit: taṃ yāntaṃ pṛṣṭhagoptāram arjunasya viśāṃ pate cāraṇāḥ prekṣya saṃhṛṣṭās tvadīyāś cāpy apūjayan
english: As he rode on, the guardian of Arjuna's rear, O lord of peoples, the Cāraṇas beheld him with delight, and even your own warriors paid him honour.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca jitvā yavanakāmbojān yuyudhānas tato 'rjunam jagāma tava sainyasya madhyena rathināṃ varaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Having conquered the Yavanas and the Kāmbojas, Yuyudhāna, that foremost of chariot-warriors, then advanced toward Arjuna through the midst of your army.

sanskrit: śaradaṃṣṭro naravyāghro vicitrakavacacchaviḥ mṛgān vyāghra ivājighraṃs tava sainyam abhīṣayat
english: That tiger among men, sharp-fanged and gleaming in his many-coloured armour, terrified your army as a tiger sniffing out deer strikes fear into them.

sanskrit: sa rathena caran mārgān dhanur abhrāmayad bhṛśam rukmapṛṣṭhaṃ mahāvegaṃ rukmacandrakasaṃkulam
english: Coursing along the paths in his chariot, he whirled his bow with great force—a bow gold-backed, mighty in might, studded with golden crescents.

sanskrit: rukmāṅgadaśirastrāṇo rukmavarmasamāvṛtaḥ rukmadhvajavaraḥ śūro meruśṛṅga ivābabhau
english: With golden armlets and golden helm, encased in golden mail, that hero of the splendid golden banner shone like a peak of Meru.

sanskrit: sadhanurmaṇḍalaḥ saṃkhye tejobhāsvararaśmivān śaradīvoditaḥ sūryo nṛsūryo virarāja ha
english: His drawn bow bent into a circle in the fray, radiant with beams of brilliant lustre, that sun among men blazed forth like the autumn sun newly risen.

sanskrit: vṛṣabhaskandhavikrānto vṛṣabhākṣo nararṣabhaḥ tāvakānāṃ babhau madhye gavāṃ madhye yathā vṛṣaḥ
english: Striding with shoulders like a bull's, bull-eyed, that bull among men shone amid your troops as a bull amid the cattle.

sanskrit: mattadviradasaṃkāśaṃ mattadviradagāminam prabhinnam iva mātaṅgaṃ yūthamadhye vyavasthitam vyāghrā iva jighāṃsantas tvadīyābhyadravan raṇe
english: Resembling a rutting elephant, moving with the gait of a rutting elephant, standing like a must elephant with temples streaming in the midst of his herd—your men, like tigers bent on the kill, rushed upon him in battle.

sanskrit: droṇānīkam atikrāntaṃ bhojānīkaṃ ca dustaram jalasaṃdhārṇavaṃ tīrtvā kāmbojānāṃ ca vāhinīm
english: He had passed through Droṇa's division and the Bhoja division, hard to cross, and had crossed the ocean-like array and the host of the Kāmbojas as one fords a flood-swollen sea.

sanskrit: hārdikyamakarān muktaṃ tīrṇaṃ vai sainyasāgaram parivavruḥ susaṃkruddhās tvadīyāḥ sātyakiṃ rathāḥ
english: As he won free of that sea of soldiers, with Hārdikya for its sea-monster, and crossed it, your chariot-warriors in great wrath encircled Sātyaki.

sanskrit: duryodhanaś citraseno duḥśāsanaviviṃśatī śakunir duḥsahaś caiva yuvā durmarṣaṇaḥ krathaḥ
english: Duryodhana, Citrasena, Duḥśāsana and Viviṃśati, Śakuni and Duḥsaha, the youth Durmarṣaṇa, and Kratha—

sanskrit: anye ca bahavaḥ śūrāḥ śastravanto durāsadāḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ sātyakiṃ yāntam anvadhāvann amarṣitāḥ
english: and many other heroes, weapon-bearing and unassailable, gave chase, enraged, to Sātyaki as he rode ahead of them.

sanskrit: atha śabdo mahān āsīt tava sainyasya māriṣa mārutoddhūtavegasya sāgarasyeva parvaṇi
english: Then there arose a mighty din from your army, O sire, like that of the sea whipped to fury by the wind on the day of the full moon.

sanskrit: tān abhidravataḥ sarvān samīkṣya śinipuṃgavaḥ śanair yāhīti yantāram abravīt prahasann iva
english: Beholding them all rushing upon him, that bull of Śini's line said to his charioteer, smiling, as it were, 'Drive on, but slowly.'

sanskrit: idam eti samuddhūtaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrasya yad balam mām evābhimukhaṃ tūrṇaṃ gajāśvarathapattimat
english: 'See how the host of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son comes surging on, straight and swift against me, with its elephants, horse, chariots, and foot.'

sanskrit: nādayan vai diśaḥ sarvā rathaghoṣeṇa sārathe pṛthivīṃ cāntarikṣaṃ ca kampayan sāgarān api
english: 'It makes all the quarters resound with the rumble of its chariots, O charioteer, and makes the earth and the sky tremble, and the very seas besides.'

sanskrit: etad balārṇavaṃ tāta vārayiṣye mahāraṇe paurṇamāsyām ivoddhūtaṃ veleva salilāśayam
english: 'This ocean of armies, my friend, I shall stem in the great battle, as the shore stems the swollen waters on the night of the full moon.'

sanskrit: paśya me sūta vikrāntam indrasyeva mahāmṛdhe eṣa sainyāni śatrūṇāṃ vidhamāmi śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: 'Behold my prowess in the great fray, O charioteer, like that of Indra; see, I scatter the armies of the foe with my whetted shafts.'

sanskrit: nihatān āhave paśya padātyaśvarathadvipān maccharair agnisaṃkāśair videhāsūn sahasraśaḥ
english: 'Behold foot, horse, chariots, and elephants slain in battle by my shafts, bright as fire, robbed of their lives by the thousand.'

sanskrit: ity evaṃ bruvatas tasya sātyaker amitaujasaḥ samīpaṃ sainikās te tu śīghram īyur yuyutsavaḥ jahy ādravasva tiṣṭheti paśya paśyeti vādinaḥ
english: As Sātyaki of measureless might spoke thus, your soldiers, eager for the fight, swiftly closed upon him, crying, 'Strike! Charge! Stand fast! Look there, look there!'

sanskrit: tān evaṃ bruvato vīrān sātyakir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ jaghāna triśatān aśvān kuñjarāṃś ca catuḥśatān
english: As those heroes shouted thus, Sātyaki with his keen shafts slew three hundred of their horses and four hundred of their elephants.

sanskrit: sa saṃprahāras tumulas tasya teṣāṃ ca dhanvinām devāsuraraṇaprakhyaḥ prāvartata janakṣayaḥ
english: That tumultuous clash between him and those bowmen, like the war of gods and demons, set in motion a great slaughter of men.

sanskrit: meghajālanibhaṃ sainyaṃ tava putrasya māriṣa pratyagṛhṇāc chineḥ pautraḥ śarair āśīviṣopamaiḥ
english: The grandson of Śini received the army of your son, dense as a mass of clouds, O sire, with shafts that were like venomous serpents.

sanskrit: pracchādyamānaḥ samare śarajālaiḥ sa vīryavān asaṃbhramaṃ mahārāja tāvakān avadhīd bahūn
english: Though veiled over in the battle by nets of arrows, that valiant one, unflustered, O great king, slew many of your warriors.

sanskrit: āścaryaṃ tatra rājendra sumahad dṛṣṭavān aham na moghaḥ sāyakaḥ kaś cit sātyaker abhavat prabho
english: A very great marvel did I behold there, O lord of kings: not one shaft of Sātyaki's, O lord, fell in vain.

sanskrit: rathanāgāśvakalilaḥ padātyūrmisamākulaḥ śaineyavelām āsādya sthitaḥ sainyamahārṇavaḥ
english: Thick with chariots, elephants, and horses, churning with waves of foot-soldiers, that vast ocean of an army, reaching the shore that was the scion of Śini, came to a halt.

sanskrit: saṃbhrāntanaranāgāśvam āvartata muhur muhuḥ tat sainyam iṣubhis tena vadhyamānaṃ samantataḥ babhrāma tatra tatraiva gāvaḥ śītārditā iva
english: With its men, elephants, and horses thrown into confusion, it wheeled about again and again; that army, smitten on every side by his arrows, milled hither and thither like cattle tormented by the cold.

sanskrit: padātinaṃ rathaṃ nāgaṃ sādinaṃ turagaṃ tathā aviddhaṃ tatra nādrākṣaṃ yuyudhānasya sāyakaiḥ
english: Footman, chariot, elephant, horseman, and horse alike—not one did I see there unpierced by the shafts of Yuyudhāna.

sanskrit: na tādṛk kadanaṃ rājan kṛtavāṃs tatra phalgunaḥ yādṛk kṣayam anīkānām akarot sātyakir nṛpa atyarjunaṃ śineḥ pautro yudhyate bharatarṣabha
english: Not such havoc, O king, did Phalguna work there as the destruction Sātyaki wrought among the divisions; the grandson of Śini fought surpassing even Arjuna, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā sātvatasya tribhiḥ śaraiḥ vivyādha sūtaṃ niśitaiś caturbhiś caturo hayān
english: Then King Duryodhana pierced the charioteer of the Sātvata with three keen shafts, and with four more his four horses.

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ ca tribhir viddhvā punar vivyādha so 'ṣṭabhiḥ duḥśāsanaḥ ṣoḍaśabhir vivyādha śinipuṃgavam
english: Having struck Sātyaki with three shafts, he pierced him again with eight, while Duḥśāsana pierced that bull of Śini's line with sixteen.

sanskrit: śakuniḥ pañcaviṃśatyā citrasenaś ca pañcabhiḥ duḥsahaḥ pañcadaśabhir vivyādhorasi sātyakim
english: Śakuni with twenty-five, Citrasena with five, and Duḥsaha with fifteen pierced Sātyaki in the breast.

sanskrit: utsmayan vṛṣṇiśārdūlas tathā bāṇaiḥ samāhataḥ tān avidhyan mahārāja sarvān eva tribhis tribhiḥ
english: That tiger of the Vṛṣṇis, smiling though thus smitten with arrows, pierced every one of them, O great king, with three shafts apiece.

sanskrit: gāḍhaviddhān arīn kṛtvā mārgaṇaiḥ so 'titejanaiḥ śaineyaḥ śyenavat saṃkhye vyacaral laghuvikramaḥ
english: Having pierced his foes deeply with those exceedingly sharp arrows, the scion of Śini ranged through the battle like a hawk, swift and nimble in his movements.

sanskrit: saubalasya dhanuś chittvā hastāvāpaṃ nikṛtya ca duryodhanaṃ tribhir bāṇair abhyavidhyat stanāntare
english: Having cut Saubala's bow and severed his leather hand-guard, he struck Duryodhana with three arrows between the breasts.

sanskrit: citrasenaṃ śatenaiva daśabhir duḥsahaṃ tathā duḥśāsanaṃ ca viṃśatyā vivyādha śinipuṃgavaḥ
english: That bull of Śini's line pierced Citrasena with a hundred shafts, Duḥsaha with ten, and Duḥśāsana with twenty.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya syālas tava viśāṃ pate aṣṭabhiḥ sātyakiṃ viddhvā punar vivyādha pañcabhiḥ
english: Then your brother-in-law, taking up another bow, O lord of peoples, pierced Sātyaki with eight shafts and again with five.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanaś ca daśabhir duḥsahaś ca tribhiḥ śaraiḥ durmukhaś ca dvādaśabhī rājan vivyādha sātyakim
english: And Duḥśāsana with ten, Duḥsaha with three shafts, and Durmukha with twelve, O king, pierced Sātyaki.

sanskrit: duryodhanas trisaptatyā viddhvā bhārata mādhavam tato 'sya niśitair bāṇais tribhir vivyādha sārathim
english: Duryodhana, O Bhārata, having pierced the Mādhava with seventy-three shafts, then struck his charioteer with three keen arrows.

sanskrit: tān sarvān sahitāñ śūrān yatamānān mahārathān pañcabhiḥ pañcabhir bāṇaiḥ punar vivyādha sātyakiḥ
english: All those heroes together, those mighty car-warriors straining their utmost, Sātyaki pierced again, each with five arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rathināṃ śreṣṭhas tava putrasya sārathim ājaghānāśu bhallena sa hato nyapatad bhuvi
english: Then that foremost of chariot-warriors swiftly struck the charioteer of your son with a broad-headed shaft, and the slain man fell to the ground.

sanskrit: pātite sārathau tasmiṃs tava putrarathaḥ prabho vātāyamānais tair aśvair apānīyata saṃgarāt
english: When that charioteer was struck down, the chariot of your son, O lord, was carried off from the field by those horses that ran like the wind.

sanskrit: tatas tava sutā rājan sainikāś ca viśāṃ pate rājño ratham abhiprekṣya vidrutāḥ śataśo 'bhavan
english: Then your sons, O king, and the soldiers, O lord of peoples, beholding the king's chariot borne away, fled by the hundreds.

sanskrit: vidrutaṃ tatra tat sainyaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhārata sātyakiḥ avākirac charais tīkṣṇai rukmapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ
english: Seeing that army in flight, O Bhārata, Sātyaki overwhelmed it with sharp arrows, gold-feathered and whetted on stone.

sanskrit: vidrāvya sarvasainyāni tāvakāni samantataḥ prayayau sātyakī rājañ śvetāśvasya rathaṃ prati
english: Having routed all your troops on every side, Sātyaki went on, O king, toward the chariot of him whose steeds were white.

sanskrit: taṃ śarān ādadānaṃ ca rakṣamāṇaṃ ca sārathim ātmānaṃ mocayantaṃ ca tāvakāḥ samapūjayan
english: As he took up his arrows, guarded his charioteer, and delivered his own self from peril, your warriors paid him honour.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca saṃpramṛdya mahat sainyaṃ yāntaṃ śaineyam arjunam nirhrīkā mama te putrāḥ kim akurvata saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When the scion of Śini, having crushed that great army, was going on toward Arjuna, what did my shameless sons do then, O Saṃjaya?

sanskrit: kathaṃ caiṣāṃ tathā yuddhe dhṛtir āsīn mumūrṣatām śaineyacaritaṃ dṛṣṭvā sadṛśaṃ savyasācinaḥ
english: And how, in such a battle, could there be any firmness left in those doomed men, when they had seen the scion of Śini bear himself like Savyasācin himself?

sanskrit: kiṃ nu vakṣyanti te kṣātraṃ sainyamadhye parājitāḥ kathaṃ ca sātyakir yuddhe vyatikrānto mahāyaśāḥ
english: What will they say of their warriorhood, vanquished there in the midst of the host? And how did Sātyaki of great renown pass them by in the battle?

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca mama putrāṇāṃ jīvatāṃ tatra saṃjaya śaineyo 'bhiyayau yuddhe tan mamācakṣva tattvataḥ
english: And how, while my sons yet lived, did the scion of Śini press on there in the fight, O Saṃjaya? Tell me that truly.

sanskrit: atyadbhutam idaṃ tāta tvatsakāśāc chṛṇomy aham ekasya bahubhir yuddhaṃ śatrubhir vai mahārathaiḥ
english: Most wondrous is this that I hear from you, my son—the battle of one man against many foes, all of them mighty car-warriors.

sanskrit: viparītam ahaṃ manye mandabhāgyān sutān prati yatrāvadhyanta samare sātvatena mahātmanā
english: I deem it an ill omen turned against my luckless sons, that they should be cut down in battle by the high-souled Sātvata.

sanskrit: ekasya hi na paryāptaṃ matsainyaṃ tasya saṃjaya kruddhasya yuyudhānasya sarve tiṣṭhantu pāṇḍavāḥ
english: For my whole army is not a match for that one man, O Saṃjaya—for Yuyudhāna in his wrath; let all the Pāṇḍavas stand aside!

sanskrit: nirjitya samare droṇaṃ kṛtinaṃ yuddhadurmadam yathā paśugaṇān siṃhas tadvad dhantā sutān mama
english: Having vanquished in battle Droṇa, the skilled, the unconquerable in war, he slays my sons as a lion slays a herd of beasts.

sanskrit: kṛtavarmādibhiḥ śūrair yattair bahubhir āhave yuyudhāno na śakito hantuṃ yaḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: By Kṛtavarman and the many other heroes, striving hard in the fray, Yuyudhāna, that bull among men, could not be slain.

sanskrit: naitad īdṛśakaṃ yuddhaṃ kṛtavāṃs tatra phalgunaḥ yādṛśaṃ kṛtavān yuddhaṃ śiner naptā mahāyaśāḥ
english: Not such a fight did Phalguna wage there as the fight that the grandson of Śini, of great renown, has waged.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tava durmantrite rājan duryodhanakṛtena ca śṛṇuṣvāvahito bhūtvā yat te vakṣyāmi bhārata
english: Saṃjaya said: This is the fruit of your ill counsel, O king, and of Duryodhana's deeds. Listen attentively to what I shall tell you, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: te punaḥ saṃnyavartanta kṛtvā saṃśaptakān mithaḥ parāṃ yuddhe matiṃ kṛtvā putrasya tava śāsanāt
english: They turned back once more, binding themselves to one another as sworn warriors, setting their hearts firmly upon battle, at the command of your son.

sanskrit: trīṇi sādisahasrāṇi duryodhanapurogamāḥ śakāḥ kāmbojabāhlīkā yavanāḥ pāradās tathā
english: Three thousand horsemen, with Duryodhana at their head—Śakas, Kāmbojas, Bāhlīkas, Yavanas, and Pāradas as well—

sanskrit: kuṇindās taṅgaṇāmbaṣṭhāḥ paiśācāś ca samandarāḥ abhyadravanta śaineyaṃ śalabhāḥ pāvakaṃ yathā
english: Kuṇindas, Taṅgaṇas, Ambaṣṭhas, and the Paiśācas together with the Mandaras—rushed upon the scion of Śini as locusts rush upon a flame.

sanskrit: yuktāś ca pārvatīyānāṃ rathāḥ pāṣāṇayodhinām śūrāḥ pañcaśatā rājañ śaineyaṃ samupādravan
english: And the harnessed chariots of the highlanders who fight with stones, five hundred heroes strong, O king, charged upon the scion of Śini.

sanskrit: tato rathasahasreṇa mahārathaśatena ca dviradānāṃ sahasreṇa dvisāhasraiś ca vājibhiḥ
english: Then with a thousand chariots and a hundred mighty car-warriors, with a thousand elephants and two thousand horses,

sanskrit: śaravarṣāṇi muñcanto vividhāni mahārathāḥ abhyadravanta śaineyam asaṃkhyeyāś ca pattayaḥ
english: those great car-warriors, loosing showers of arrows of every kind, rushed upon the scion of Śini, together with footmen past counting.

sanskrit: tāṃś ca saṃcodayan sarvān ghnatainam iti bhārata duḥśāsano mahārāja sātyaktiṃ paryavārayat
english: Urging them all on with the cry 'Slay him!', O Bhārata, Duḥśāsana, O great king, hemmed Sātyaki round about.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma śaineyacaritaṃ mahat yad eko bahubhiḥ sārdham asaṃbhrāntam ayudhyata
english: There we beheld the great and wondrous feat of the scion of Śini—that he alone fought, unflinching, against so many.

sanskrit: avadhīc ca rathānīkaṃ dviradānāṃ ca tad balam sādinaś caiva tān sarvān dasyūn api ca sarvaśaḥ
english: He slew the chariot-division and that force of elephants, and all the horsemen, and the barbarians too, every one of them.

sanskrit: tatra cakrair vimathitair bhagnaiś ca paramāyudhaiḥ akṣaiś ca bahudhā bhagnair īṣādaṇḍakabandhuraiḥ
english: There, with wheels crushed and the finest weapons shattered, with axles broken in many places, and shafts, poles, and chariot-frames,

sanskrit: kūbarair mathitaiś cāpi dhvajaiś cāpi nipātitaiḥ varmabhiś cāmaraiś caiva vyavakīrṇā vasuṃdharā
english: with splintered chariot-poles and banners struck down, with coats of mail and yak-tail whisks, the earth lay all bestrewn.

sanskrit: sragbhir ābharaṇair vastrair anukarṣaiś ca māriṣa saṃchannā vasudhā tatra dyaur grahair iva bhārata
english: With garlands, ornaments, garments, and chariot-trappings, O sire, the earth was covered over there, as the sky is covered with planets, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: girirūpadharāś cāpi patitāḥ kuñjarottamāḥ añjanasya kule jātā vāmanasya ca bhārata supratīkakule jātā mahāpadmakule tathā
english: And lordly elephants, mountain-like in form, lay fallen—born of the line of Añjana and of Vāmana, O Bhārata, born of the line of Supratīka and of the line of Mahāpadma as well,

sanskrit: airāvaṇakule caiva tathānyeṣu kuleṣu ca jātā dantivarā rājañ śerate bahavo hatāḥ
english: and of the line of Airāvaṇa, and of yet other lines as well—those choicest of tuskers, O king, lay there slain in great numbers.

sanskrit: vanāyujān pārvatīyān kāmbojāraṭṭabāhlikān tathā hayavarān rājan nijaghne tatra sātyakiḥ
english: Horses of the finest breed—from Vanāyu, from the hill-country, from Kāmboja, Āraṭṭa, and Bāhlika—Sātyaki slew there, O king.

sanskrit: nānādeśasamutthāṃś ca nānājātyāṃś ca pattinaḥ nijaghne tatra śaineyaḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: And footmen sprung from many lands and of many races the scion of Śini slew there by the hundreds and by the thousands.

sanskrit: teṣu prakālyamāneṣu dasyūn duḥśāsano 'bravīt nivartadhvam adharmajñā yudhyadhvaṃ kiṃ sṛtena vaḥ
english: As they were being driven before him, Duḥśāsana said to the barbarians, 'Turn back, you who know no law! Fight on! What good is your fleeing?'

sanskrit: tāṃś cāpi sarvān saṃprekṣya putro duḥśāsanas tava pāṣāṇayodhinaḥ śūrān pārvatīyān acodayat
english: And looking upon them all, your son Duḥśāsana spurred on the highland heroes who fought with stones.

sanskrit: aśmayuddheṣu kuśalā naitaj jānāti sātyakiḥ aśmayuddham ajānantaṃ ghnatainaṃ yuddhakāmukam
english: 'You are skilled in battle with stones; this Sātyaki knows it not. He knows not stone-warfare—slay him, this man so eager for the fight!'

sanskrit: tathaiva kuravaḥ sarve nāśmayuddhaviśāradāḥ abhidravata mā bhaiṣṭa na vaḥ prāpsyati sātyakiḥ
english: 'Just so, none of the Kurus are versed in battle with stones. Charge on, fear not! Sātyaki shall not overtake you.'
